text.div: An adverse event (AE) is any untoward medical occurrence in a clinical trial participant administered a medicinal product, which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with this treatment.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 9.1.1 Definitions of Adverse Events

text.div: A serious adverse event (SAE) is any untoward medical occurrence that results in death, is life-threatening, requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation, results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity, or is a congenital anomaly or birth defect.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 9.1.2 Definitions of Serious Adverse Events

text.div: A product complaint is any written, electronic, or oral communication that alleges deficiencies related to the identity, quality, durability, reliability, safety, effectiveness, or performance of a medicinal product.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 9.1.3 Definitions of Product Complaints

text.div: A medical device product complaint is any written, electronic, or oral communication that alleges deficiencies related to the identity, quality, durability, reliability, safety, effectiveness, or performance of a medical device.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 9.1.3.1 Definitions of Medical Device Product Complaints
ICH M11 Protocol Section 9.2 Timing and Procedures for Collection and Reporting

text.div: All adverse events will be collected from the time of informed consent until the end of the follow-up period as specified in the Schedule of Activities.
Adverse events will be identified through participant self-report, clinician observation, and review of clinical assessments at each visit.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 9.2.2.1 Collection Procedures: Identification

text.div: The severity of adverse events will be graded according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5.0.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 9.2.2.2 Collection Procedures: Severity

text.div: The causal relationship between each adverse event and the investigational product will be assessed by the investigator as either related or not related.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 9.2.2.3 Collection Procedures: Causality
ICH M11 Protocol Section 9.2.2.4 Collection Procedures: Recording

text.div: All adverse events will be recorded in the electronic case report form within 24 hours of the investigator becoming aware of the event.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 9.2.2.5 Collection Procedures: Follow-up

text.div: Serious adverse events must be reported to the sponsor within 24 hours of the investigator becoming aware of the event.
The sponsor will report all suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions (SUSARs) to the relevant regulatory authorities in accordance with local requirements.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 9.2.3.1 Regulatory Reporting Requirements

ICH M11 Protocol Section 9.2.5 Disease-related Events or Outcomes Not Qualifying as AEs or SAEs

text.div: Female participants who become pregnant during the trial must be withdrawn from investigational product. Pregnancy outcomes will be followed up and reported.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 9.3.1 Participants Who Become Pregnant During the Trial

text.div: If a male participant's partner becomes pregnant during the trial or within 90 days of the last dose, the participant must notify the investigator who will report the pregnancy to the sponsor.
